title: “Monks, just as a young man or woman, youthful, fond of adornment, would be distressed, ashamed, and disgusted if the carcass of a snake, a…
content: “Monks, just as a young man or woman, youthful, fond of adornment, would be distressed, ashamed, and disgusted if the carcass of a snake, a dog, or a human were hung around their neck; so too, monks, that monk, examining the peril in those thoughts … the mind becomes steadied, settled, unified, and concentrated.”

title: One with craving as companion Wanders for a long time — Now here, now there — He cannot stop The wandering of rebirth. Having understood…
content:
One with craving as companion
Wanders for a long time —
Now here, now there —
He cannot stop
The wandering of rebirth.
Having understood this danger —
That craving is the origin of suffering —
The monk, abandoning craving,
Not grasping, not clinging,
Mindfully dwells,
Living the homeless life.

title: Elder Kulla: Kulla went to the charnel ground, Saw a woman abandoned, Thrown away in the cemetery, Food for worms. “Kulla, look at this body…
content:
Elder Kulla:

Kulla went to the charnel ground,
Saw a woman abandoned,
Thrown away in the cemetery,
Food for worms.

“Kulla, look at this body —
Diseased, foul, stinking,
Oozing, seeping,
Delighting fools.”

Having taken up the mirror of Dhamma,
I attained right view.
I contemplated this body —
Empty inside and out.

As it is below, so above,
As above, so below,
As below, so above,
As above, so below.

As by day, so by night,
As by night, so by day,
As before, so after,
As after, so before.

Such a one does not delight
In the five kinds of music.
When one-pointed,
Rightly meditating on the Dhamma.

title: “Monks, these three are inner stains, inner enemies, inner foes, inner murderers, inner adversaries. What three? Greed, monks, is an inner stain, inner enemy, inner…
content: “Monks, these three are inner stains, inner enemies, inner foes, inner murderers, inner adversaries. What three? Greed, monks, is an inner stain, inner enemy, inner foe, inner murderer, inner adversary. Hatred, monks, is an inner stain … Delusion, monks, is an inner stain, inner enemy, inner foe, inner murderer, inner adversary. These, monks, are the three inner stains, inner enemies, inner foes, inner murderers, inner adversaries.”

title: “Monks, I will teach about suffering and the root of suffering. Listen … And what, monks, is suffering? Form, monks, is suffering; feeling is suffering;…
content: “Monks, I will teach about suffering and the root of suffering. Listen … And what, monks, is suffering? Form, monks, is suffering; feeling is suffering; perception is suffering; formations are suffering; consciousness is suffering. This, monks, is called suffering. And what, monks, is the root of suffering? It is this craving that leads to renewed existence, accompanied by delight and lust, delighting here and there — that is, craving for sensual pleasures, craving for existence, craving for non-existence.”

title: “Monks, just as an oil lamp burns in dependence on oil and a wick, and someone occasionally pours in oil and adjusts the wick —…
content: “Monks, just as an oil lamp burns in dependence on oil and a wick, and someone occasionally pours in oil and adjusts the wick — that oil lamp, being nourished and sustained in such a way, would burn for a long time. So too, monks, one who dwells seeing gratification in things that are fetters — craving increases. With craving as condition, clinging arises … Thus the origination of this whole mass of suffering. Monks, just as an oil lamp burns in dependence on oil and a wick, and no one occasionally pours in oil or adjusts the wick — that oil lamp, being without its own fuel, with no further fuel added, not being nourished, would be extinguished. So too, monks, one who dwells seeing peril in things that are fetters — craving ceases. With the cessation of craving, clinging ceases … Thus the cessation of this whole mass of suffering.”

title: “Migajāla, there are phenomena cognizable by the mind that are desirable … enticing. If a monk does not delight in them, does not praise them,…
content: “Migajāla, there are phenomena cognizable by the mind that are desirable … enticing. If a monk does not delight in them, does not praise them, and dwells without lust for them, then delight ceases. With the cessation of delight, lust ceases. With the cessation of lust, bondage ceases. Not being bound by the bondage of delight, Migajāla, that monk is called ‘one who dwells alone.’ Even if he lives in the midst of a village crowded with monks, nuns, laymen, laywomen, kings, royal ministers, ascetics of other sects and their disciples — still he is called ‘one who dwells alone.’ Why? Because craving, the companion, has been abandoned by him. Therefore he is called ‘one who dwells alone.’”

title: Sitting down to one side, those monks said to the Blessed One: - Here, venerable sir, King Pasenadi of Kosala has had many people bound.…
content:
Sitting down to one side, those monks said to the Blessed One:
- Here, venerable sir, King Pasenadi of Kosala has had many people bound. Some are bound with ropes, some with chains, some with shackles.

Then the Blessed One, understanding the meaning of this, on that occasion recited this verse:
The wise say that such binding
Is not strong —
Binding with iron, with ropes,
With wooden shackles —
But infatuation with sensual pleasures,
With jewels and ornaments,
And anxious thoughts
Directed toward children and wives —
The wise say this binding
Is truly strong.
Though it drags one down,
Subtle and hard to escape,
True renunciants cut it in two,
Without wishing or longing,
Abandoning all sensual pleasures.

title: “Ānanda, those noble thoughts that are conducive to progress and lead to the complete destruction of suffering — such as renunciation thoughts, non-ill-will thoughts, harmlessness…
content: “Ānanda, those noble thoughts that are conducive to progress and lead to the complete destruction of suffering — such as renunciation thoughts, non-ill-will thoughts, harmlessness thoughts — he reflects: ‘I will think these thoughts.’ In this way, he is clearly aware of that.”

title: “I do not see any other thing, monks, that so prevents unarisen sensual desire from arising, or abandons arisen sensual desire, as the sign of…
content: “I do not see any other thing, monks, that so prevents unarisen sensual desire from arising, or abandons arisen sensual desire, as the sign of the foul. The sign of the foul, monks, when wisely attended to, prevents unarisen sensual desire from arising and abandons arisen sensual desire.”
